---
title: "Get an overview of Zenodo deposits"
description: |
  Use the `list` and `get` commands to retrieve existing Zenodo deposits and find deposits matching a metadata file.
order: 4
---

The `list` and `get` commands can be used to retrieve information about existing
Zenodo deposits. While `list` retrieves all deposits associated with the
authenticated Zenodo account, `get` finds the deposit matching a specific
`zendo_id` archived in the `.zenodo.toml` file.

Both commands are useful for checking whether a deposit already exists and
retrieving information about it before performing operations such as `update` or
`publish`.

### Listing deposits

The `list` command retrieve all deposits associated with your Zenodo
authentication token.

To list deposits in the main Zenodo environment, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do list
```

The optional --sandbox argument retrieves deposits from the Zenodo sandbox
environment instead of the main Zenodo environment:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do list --sandbox
```

### Getting a deposit

While `list` will list *all* deposits, the `get` command only retrieves the
Zenodo deposit JSON for a unique deposit matching the `zendo_id`. This ID is
stored in the `.zenodo.toml` file.

The command takes one optional argument: the path to the metadata file. If no
path is provided, it defaults to `.zenodo.toml` in the working directory.

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get [METADATA_FILE] --sandbox
```

The command searches the deposits associated with the authenticated Zenodo
account and identifies a matching deposit using the `zendo_id`. If a matching
deposit is found, its deposit JSON is returned.

For example, to retrieve the deposit associated with the default `.zenodo.toml`
file, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get
```

To search for the deposit in the Zenodo sandbox environment, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get --sandbox
```
